from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Algebraic Dot Product", 
                          ["Dot product sums element-wise products.", 
                           "It measures shared directional alignment.", 
                           "Imagine a grocery list example."])
        
        # Assets
        grocery_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grocery.svg")
        cart_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cart.svg")
        
        # --- Pre-calculate elements ---
        formula = MathTex(r"\vec{v} \cdot \vec{w} = \sum v_i w_i", color=WHITE)
        formula2 = MathTex(r"\vec{v} \cdot \vec{w} = \|\vec{v}\| \|\vec{w}\| \cos(\theta)", color=WHITE)
        term_to_highlight = MathTex(r"\|\vec{v}\| \cos(\theta)", color=YELLOW)
        
        vec_v = Vector([1.5, 1.0], color=BLUE)
        line = Line([-1, -0.25, 0], [3, 0.75, 0], color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B3', 'C4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_at_grid(grocery_icon, "A3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(formula), FadeIn(grocery_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(grocery_icon))
        
        self.place_in_area(formula2, 'B3', 'C4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(formula2))
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(formula2))
        self.place_at_grid(term_to_highlight, 'D3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(cart_icon, "D5", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Write(term_to_highlight), FadeIn(cart_icon))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeOut(term_to_highlight), FadeOut(cart_icon))
        
        self.place_in_area(line, 'E3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_v, "E3", scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(line), GrowArrow(vec_v))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis: The Geometry of Duality", [
            "Linear functions correspond to unique vectors.",
            "The normal vector is the function's dual.",
            "Rotating vectors rotates the associated plane."
        ])
        
        # Setup visual elements
        plane_color = "#3498db"
        vector_color = "#e74c3c"
        
        # Load assets
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg")
        protractor = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/protractor.svg")
        
        # Initial Line (Plane) and Normal
        line = Line(start=np.array([-1, 0, 0]), end=np.array([1, 0, 0]), color=plane_color)
        normal = Vector(direction=np.array([0, 1, 0]), color=vector_color)
        
        # Combine into a group for consistent positioning
        animation_group = VGroup(line, normal, ruler, protractor)
        
        # Position in grid as per VideoCritic instructions
        self.place_in_area(animation_group, 'C4', 'D5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(normal, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Tracking variables
        angle = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # Updates
        # Apply rotation to the line around its center
        line.add_updater(lambda m: m.rotate(angle.get_value() - m.get_angle()))
        # Normal rotates based on line + PI/2
        normal.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(angle.get_value() + PI/2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(plane_color))
        self.play(FadeIn(ruler), Create(line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(vector_color))
        self.play(GrowArrow(normal))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#f1c40f"))
        self.play(FadeIn(protractor))
        self.play(angle.animate.set_value(PI/2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Geometry of Dot Products and Duality

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Algebraic Dot Product
sections.content: Briefly define the dot product as the sum of element-wise products (a · b = Σ a_i b_i). Visualize this as a 'matching' operation: how much do two vectors point in the same direction?
sections.example: Comparing two grocery lists: Vector A (quantities purchased) vs. Vector B (unit prices). The dot product gives the total cost.

sections.title: Visualizing Projections
sections.content: Shift to the geometric definition: a · b = |a||b|cos(θ). Animate vector 'a' casting a shadow onto vector 'b'. Emphasize that the dot product is the length of one vector projected onto another, scaled by the second vector's length.
sections.example: A hiker pulling a wagon: Only the component of force in the direction of movement contributes to the work done.

sections.title: The Concept of Duality
sections.content: Introduce duality: A dot product with a fixed vector 'v' can be viewed as a 'function' (linear map) that turns any input vector 'u' into a scalar. Visualize the fixed vector 'v' as defining a 'level set' of parallel lines (or planes).
sections.example: A 'Sensor' vector: Imagine a laser grid. A vector passing through the grid triggers a reading based on its alignment with the grid lines; the grid defines the linear function.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Geometry of Duality
sections.content: Explain that every linear function (a plane) in space corresponds to a unique vector (its normal). The vector is the 'dual' of the plane. Show an animation where rotating a normal vector perfectly rotates the associated plane.
sections.example: A 2D character (a robot) trying to detect if an object is 'in front' of its field of view. The robot's 'line of sight' vector is the dual to the boundary line dividing 'safe' from 'danger' zones.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize: The dot product is not just math; it is a tool for measuring alignment and projecting points onto boundaries. Duality is the bridge between a 'direction' and the 'slice' it creates.
sections.example: In machine learning (SVMs), the 'dual' vector defines the decision boundary that classifies cat vs. dog images.
